title: Defence: signals and second and third hand

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 7, case 1

problems.explanation: Partner's ace promises the king. You hold the ♥Q, so partner can cash the K and lead a third heart to your Q: you'd like hearts continued. A high spot card encourages: play the ♥8.

whyNot.H3: A low spot card discourages. Partner might switch, and your side would lose its third heart trick.
whyNot.HQ: Partner's A and K win the first two tricks anyway. Keep the Q to win the third.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 7, case 2

problems.explanation: Without the ♥Q, you don't want partner to go on: if declarer has the Q, cashing the K sets it up, but if you wait, declarer may never make it. A low spot card discourages: play the ♥3.

whyNot.H8: A high spot card encourages, and partner would cash the K, setting up declarer's Q.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 9

problems.explanation: With two cards, play high then low. The ♥8 encourages: partner cashes the K, you follow with the 3, and partner leads a third heart for you to ruff.

whyNot.H3: Low discourages, and you'd miss the ruff. With a doubleton, play the higher card first.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 13, hand 2
reviewNotes: The handout doesn't show dummy; the dummy here is chosen to fit.

problems.explanation: Three small cards and no honour: nothing to encourage. Play your lowest, the ♥3, to discourage.

whyNot.H8: The 8 is a high spot card: it would encourage partner to continue.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 13, hand 4
reviewNotes: The handout doesn't show dummy; the dummy here is chosen to fit.

problems.explanation: Partner's ♥K promises the Q, and you have the J: together you hold K Q J, so hearts are safe to continue. Encourage with a high spot card: the ♥8.

whyNot.H3: Low discourages. With the J completing partner's sequence, you want hearts.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 13, hand 5
reviewNotes: The handout doesn't show dummy; the dummy here is chosen to fit.

problems.explanation: Partner's ♥Q promises the J. With no honour to help, discourage with your lowest card: the ♥3.

whyNot.H8: A high spot card would ask partner to continue, with nothing to back it up.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 13, hand 6
reviewNotes: The handout doesn't show dummy; the dummy here is chosen to fit.

problems.explanation: Partner's ♥Q promises the J, and you have the K: hearts are your side's suit. Encourage with a high spot card, the ♥8, and keep the K.

whyNot.HK: Don't play your K on partner's Q: the Q will win if declarer doesn't take it, and the K is worth keeping.
whyNot.H3: Low discourages, but you want hearts continued.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 12

problems.explanation: Signals aren't only for when partner's card wins. Partner's ♦K promises the Q, and dummy took the A. With the ♦J, you know it's safe for partner to continue diamonds later: encourage with the ♦8.

whyNot.D3: Low discourages. Your J makes diamonds a good suit for partner to attack again.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 16

problems.explanation: With a doubleton, start high-low: the ♦5, then the 2. The 5 doesn't look high, but partner, seeing the 2 missing, should read it as encouraging, cash the K and give you a ruff.

whyNot.D2: Your lowest card discourages, and you'd miss the ruff. Start a high-low with the 5.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 17
reviewNotes: The handout states the rule without an example; the cards here are chosen to fit.

problems.explanation: The exception: with Q x under partner's ace, play the small card. Playing the Q under the ace promises the J (or a singleton), and partner would underlead the K to your 'J'.

whyNot.CQ: The Q under partner's ace shows the J as well, or a singleton. With Q x, play the x.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 23

problems.explanation: Think about dummy's ♦Q. If partner continues with the K, the Q becomes good for declarer, who'll throw a loser on it. If partner switches, declarer never makes the Q. So discourage, even with the J: play the ♦2.

whyNot.D8: Encouraging asks partner to cash the K, setting up dummy's Q for a discard.

deals.source: Phil Abrahamson, “10 Attitude Signals on Defense”, page 18
reviewNotes: The handout writes small cards as x; the spot cards here are chosen to keep its point.
In the handout, partner wins this trick with the ♠A; whether declarer would lead the K into it doesn't matter for the discard.

problems.explanation: You can't follow to the spade, so your discard can signal. You'd love partner to lead a heart through dummy's K J to your A Q. A high spot card in a suit asks for it: discard the ♥7.

acceptable.D2: A low spot card says you don't want a suit, which also points partner away from diamonds.

whyNot.H2: A low heart says you don't want hearts: the opposite of what you mean.
whyNot.HA: Throwing the A gives away a sure trick.

problems.explanation: Second hand low. Declarer leads towards dummy's Q: if you play low, declarer's K (if they have it) and dummy's Q can't both win, because your A kills one of them. And if partner has the K, partner takes the Q.

whyNot.HA: Rising with the A sets up both dummy's Q and declarer's K: two tricks instead of one.
whyNot.HJ: Splitting your honours gives declarer a cheap trick. Play low.

problems.explanation: Second hand low, in tempo. If you play low smoothly, declarer has to guess between the K and the J, and may guess wrong. If you hesitate, declarer knows you're thinking about the A and plays the K.

whyNot.HA: Rising with the A sets up dummy's K and J. Keep it to capture an honour later.

problems.explanation: Cover an honour with an honour. If you play low, declarer lets the Q run, then leads towards the A J, and your K dies anyway. Covering kills the Q with your K, and partner's 10 may become a winner.

whyNot.H4: Declarer's Q wins, and your K is caught on the next round.

problems.explanation: Third hand high: you're the last chance to win the trick for your side. Partner led low, so partner doesn't have the K Q. Win the ♥A and lead back to partner's honours: partner may have the K, or the Q sitting over declarer.

whyNot.H9: If declarer has the K or Q, playing low lets declarer win a cheap trick.

problems.explanation: Third hand high: play the ♠Q. Partner led low, so partner doesn't have the A. If declarer takes the Q with the A, partner's K (or J) is set up for later.

whyNot.S9: Declarer could win cheaply with the J or 10.

problems.explanation: Third hand high, but the lowest of touching cards: the ♦10. If declarer wins with the A, partner knows you have the Q and J (declarer would have won with them otherwise), and keeps attacking diamonds.

whyNot.DQ: From touching cards, play the lowest. The Q would tell partner declarer has the J, and partner might stop leading the suit.

problems.explanation: Think before playing third hand high. Partner's ♥J promises the 10, so declarer has the Q. If you take the A now, dummy's K and declarer's Q are both good. Keep the A to kill the K later, and encourage with the ♥9.

whyNot.HA: Winning the A sets up two heart tricks for declarer: dummy's K and the Q.
whyNot.H2: Low discourages, but you want partner to continue hearts through dummy's K.
